gap: No result ChatGPT got states that UGREEN NASync boxes have a BIOS watchdog that keeps rebooting a non-UGOS OS such as Proxmox, TrueNAS or Unraid until it is turned off in the BIOS (Ctrl+F12 at the UGREEN logo), or that UGREEN's policy leaves the hardware warranty unchanged when you install a third-party system.
standout_why: I compared against proxmox.com requirements (cited in all three chats), homelabpicks.com/nas/best-nas-for-proxmox and computingforgeeks.com/best-nas-for-proxmox. Proxmox's page names no NAS vendor and covers no install steps. Homelabpicks covers TerraMaster, QNAP TS-464, ASUSTOR and Synology, never mentions a watchdog, and has nothing on UGREEN's warranty stance. Computingforgeeks tested Proxmox as an NFS or iSCSI client of the NAS and never covers installing Proxmox on the NAS itself. The ChatGPT answer of 2026-11-08 12:16 mentions 'watchdog quirks' in passing, but none of its sources says what the watchdog does, how to turn it off, or how the warranty is affected.
decides: This confirms the UGREEN DXP4800 Plus or DXP6800 Pro as the all-in-one Proxmox pick. Bare-metal Proxmox works once the watchdog is off, and per UGREEN's policy as the Debian wiki quotes it, the hardware warranty is unchanged. By contrast, homelabpicks says TerraMaster voids the warranty when you install another OS, and QNAP's TVS-h674 page lists only QTS and QuTS hero and says to use only QNAP memory. Where Proxmox is the main goal, this tips the choice toward UGREEN over TerraMaster.

findings.label: BIOS watchdog under a third-party OS
findings.value: Turn off the watchdog in the BIOS, save and reboot before installing; otherwise the box reboots on its own
findings.note: The Debian wiki install steps say to turn off the watchdog in the BIOS and to turn off the eMMC controller so the UGREEN installer does not boot. Tested models listed: DXP2800, DXP4800, DXP8800 Plus. Page last edited 2026-01-31.

findings.label: Watchdog and BIOS access, named reviewer
findings.value: Ctrl+F12 at the UGREEN logo opens the BIOS; with the watchdog left on, 'Unraid will randomly reboot'
findings.source_title: How to install Unraid on a Ugreen NASync DXP4800 Plus (Mighty Gadget, James Smythe)
findings.note: Published 2025-12-24, updated 2026-07-03. Smythe also suggests turning off the stock UGOS NVMe drive (SSD2 on his unit) in the BIOS. His spec table gives 8 GB DDR5 standard and 64 GB maximum.

findings.label: Warranty with a third-party OS (UGREEN policy as quoted)
findings.value: 'If you choose to install a third-party system, there might be unknown compatibility issues. The official hardware warranty policy will remain unchanged.'
findings.note: The wiki quotes UGREEN but gives no link. UGREEN's own warranty page (ai.ugreen.com/pages/warranty) returned HTTP 429 on every try, so I could not read this on the maker's page. NASCompares' Q&A of 2024-03-14 (https://nascompares.com/guide/ugreen-brand-user-qa-questions-about-the-new-nasync-nas-storage-solution/, read 2026-11-08) quotes an earlier UGREEN answer: 'they will lose the warranty permanently'. A comment on that page dated 2024-03-26 reports that UGREEN later said its warranty policy 'will not change'. Only cite the policy as a direct UGREEN quote after opening UGREEN's page.

findings.label: Memory compatibility and OS
findings.value: 64 GB max (2× 32 GB DDR4 SO-DIMM); 'Use only QNAP memory modules'; unsupported modules 'may ... prevent the operating system from starting'; OS listed: QTS 6.1.0 / QuTS hero h6.1.0
findings.note: The page does not say whether ECC is supported. Virtualization Station needs at least 4 GB RAM and QNAP suggests up to 12 VMs, 'may vary by the memory installed'. Warranty: 3 years. Two M.2 2280 PCIe Gen4 x4 slots; PCIe Gen4 x16 + Gen4 x4 slots; 2× 2.5GbE, with 10GbE only by add-in card.

findings.value: Proxmox VE 9.0 saw the drives and the onboard NICs (Marvell AQC113 10GbE, Realtek RTL8126 5GbE); an add-in Realtek RTL8127 10GbE card needed drivers added

findings.note: ServeTheHome says the Pro has 'ECC memory support' but does not say whether Proxmox or EDAC reports ECC. The article has no SATA passthrough or IOMMU test.

unsourced: UGREEN's own warranty page and help center (ai.ugreen.com/pages/warranty, ai-uk.ugreen.com/pages/product-warranty, www.ugreen.com/pages/warranty, support.ugnas.com/detail/article/en-US/133): all returned HTTP 429 or a JS-only shell, so the third-party OS statement and per-model warranty years are not read on the maker's page. A search snippet suggested 3 years for the DXP6800 and DXP8800 against 2 years for the others; I could not open a page to confirm it, and it conflicts with our page's '2 years' for the DXP6800 Pro.

The exact BIOS menu location for the watchdog and how often it reboots: a search snippet mentioned a 3-minute reboot and an 'Advanced → Watchdog Settings' or 'FAST' tab, but neither page I opened (Debian wiki, Mighty Gadget) states either.

Which SATA controller the bays use on the DXP4800 Plus and DXP6800 Pro, and whether it sits alone in an IOMMU group for passing through to a TrueNAS VM: no maker document, manual or named reviewer found within budget.
